source.version: arXiv:2503.01631v1 [cs.HC], 3 Mar 2025, as stamped on PDF p. 1; typeset as the CHI ’25 paper with DOI 10.1145/3706598.3713273. The ACM version of record was not inspected.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A-E in the same PDF (PDF pp. 17-25); no separate supplement used.

studies.label: Main online experiment (problem reframing, four conditions)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6, Figure 4 caption and Section 4.2; PDF p. 9, Figure 8, right-hand table, Total column
counts_source.quote: 456 participants ... 280 participants ... MANUAL (baseline) 62 (36, 10) ... DIRECT 72 (35, 12) ... STRUCTURED 88 (33, 10) ... FREE-FORM 58 (34, 9)

arms.name: MANUAL
arms.description: Baseline: participants reframe the design problem by themselves without an LLM (PDF p. 5, Figure 3 and Section 4).

arms.name: DIRECT
arms.description: Participants press a button to generate or regenerate GPT-4o problem frames from standardized prompts and may submit or build on them; ideas_supplied (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3; PDF p. 17, Appendix A.1).

arms.name: STRUCTURED
arms.description: A button interface guides GPT-4o through Dorst’s nine-step process, supplying intermediate content and final frames; participants can regenerate content or add their own; ideas_supplied (PDF p. 19, Appendix A.2; PDF p. 20, Figure 14).

arms.name: FREE-FORM
arms.description: Participants converse freely with default ChatGPT (GPT-4o) using their own accounts and submit the conversation log; open_chat (PDF p. 7, Section 4.5).

studies.task: Reframe an assigned design problem about aging, littering, or conflicting lunch preferences into two novel and useful alternative frames using a common template, then select the preferred frame for expert evaluation (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 4.3-4.5).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-4o; FREE-FORM used the default version of ChatGPT (GPT-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1 (GPT-4o; experiment in August 2024); PDF p. 7, Section 4.5 (default ChatGPT and the same GPT-4o model for all users). The model release year is not explicitly stated.

estimates.outcome: Novelty of the selected problem frame (expert rated)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: 15 expert designers selected from the study participants using their pre-survey understanding of problem reframing rated other participants’ selected frames, blind to condition (PDF p. 5, Section 4.1; PDF p. 8, Section 4.5). Each rater reviewed 36 randomly sampled frames balanced across approaches and problems (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). Questionnaires assessed the perspective’s novelty and usefulness relative to the original problem. Scale anchors, ratings per frame, and rating aggregation are not specified.

estimates.notes: The paper calls this pooled arm LLM-ALL. The reported bound covers novelty and usefulness for LLM-ALL versus MANUAL and the across-approach analysis; it is not an exact p-value. Mann-Whitney U is named, but its statistic is not printed. The participant basis follows the stated analysis of one selected frame per participant; how repeated expert ratings were aggregated is unreported. Figure 5 (PDF p. 8) gives unlabeled box plots only: no arm means, SDs, SEs, differences, confidence intervals, or standardized effects are transcribed or estimated from the plot. Arm sample sizes are the printed analyzed counts, not randomized counts. Parentheses in the Figure 8 count-table cells contain age means and SDs, not outcome statistics.

estimates.notes: Retained as a full-sample contrast listed in the reconciled screening form and described by the paper’s blanket across-approach conclusion. The paper names a Kruskal-Wallis test and Dunn’s post-hoc procedure with Bonferroni correction (PDF p. 8, Section 5), but prints no result for this specific pair. The blanket bound is not assigned as this pair’s p-value, and no omnibus statistic is assigned to the pair. No contrast-specific uncertainty is reported. Combined people and output totals for this pair are not printed and have not been computed. Figure 5 (PDF p. 8) gives unlabeled box plots only: no arm means, SDs, SEs, differences, confidence intervals, or standardized effects are transcribed or estimated from the plot. Arm sample sizes are the printed analyzed counts, not randomized counts. Parentheses in the Figure 8 count-table cells contain age means and SDs, not outcome statistics. This AI arm is the closest to free use of a general chatbot under codebook section 8; the paper still supplies no pair-specific statistic.

not_extracted.reason: Self-reported helpfulness of the LLM system for creative activity, not an evaluation of the generated frames (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 10, Section 5.4; PDF pp. 10-11, Figure 9 and Section 5.5).

not_extracted.reason: Self-reported perceived workload/effort, not creativity of produced output (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF pp. 9-10, Figure 7 and Section 5.4; PDF pp. 10-11, Figure 9 and Section 5.5).

not_extracted.reason: Attitudes and qualitative self-reports, including participants’ judgments of AI-generated material, rather than independent scores on participants’ produced frames (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF pp. 9-10, Sections 5.2-5.4).
Task duration is a process/productivity measure, not an outcome scored on creative output (PDF p. 8, Section 5).

not_extracted.what: S1: regeneration of LLM-generated content and frames
not_extracted.reason: Tool-use behavior and counts of model generations, not human-output fluency or another scored creative-output outcome (PDF p. 8, Section 5).

not_extracted.what: S1: problem-reframing knowledge quiz and expertise balance test
not_extracted.reason: The quiz was administered before the reframing treatment and used to classify expertise and select raters; it is not a post-treatment convergent outcome (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 4.4-4.5; PDF pp. 10-11, Section 5.5; PDF p. 24, Appendix B).

not_extracted.what: S1: novelty comparisons between experts and novices
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup/expertise comparisons; expertise was measured rather than randomized. These are not full-sample AI-versus-comparison contrasts (PDF pp. 10-12, Section 5.5 and Figure 10).

not_extracted.what: S1: usefulness comparisons between experts and novices
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup/expertise comparisons; expertise was measured rather than randomized. These are not full-sample AI-versus-comparison contrasts (PDF pp. 10-12, Section 5.5 and Figure 10).

not_extracted.what: S2: pilot study of problem-reframing feasibility
not_extracted.reason: Below the codebook minimum sample: Appendix D says "we recruited 36 people". The authors internally reviewed frame quality but report no condition-specific outcome or contrast. Pilot-specific model and interface details are not established (PDF p. 25, Appendix D).

open_items: No full-sample arm means, outcome SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, standardized effects, or numerical test statistics for novelty or usefulness are printed. Figure 5 contains unlabeled box plots only (PDF p. 8).

No pair-specific result is printed for any individual-arm contrast. The blanket all-p-above-threshold result in Section 5.2 is not a separately reported Dunn comparison. Pairwise p_value and test fields therefore remain null (PDF pp. 8-9).

Rating scale anchors, number of ratings per frame, and aggregation across expert raters are not reported. The pooled se_basis follows the stated one-frame-per-participant analysis, but the treatment of repeated ratings requires clarification (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 4.3-5).

Per-arm randomized counts and per-arm exclusions are missing. The analysis excludes people failing attention/format/time checks and excludes LLM-arm non-users after assignment; it is not an intention-to-treat analysis (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2).
The cited PDF is the arXiv manuscript, while the citation record identifies a later ACM version of record. Differences from that version have not been established.
The experiment used GPT-4o in August 2024, but the paper does not explicitly state the model release year; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 2, Section 1).
notes: The complete markdown conversion, including references and appendices, was read, and every cited PDF page was checked with PyMuPDF. Only the eligible main experiment is in studies; the smaller pilot is in not_extracted. The study is an individually randomized between-participant design using balanced Latin square assignment (PDF p. 5, Section 4.1). Novelty and usefulness are the paper’s primary hypothesis outcomes (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1), but preregistration is not stated. DIRECT and STRUCTURED supply generated ideas, while FREE-FORM permits open chat, so the study-level ai_role is other. No across-people diversity or after-AI outcome is reported. No shared sample with another paper is identified in the screening form. All paired-arm totals left null are unprinted; no counts or effects were calculated. The Figure 8 right-hand table is printed numeric tabular data, not values estimated from a plot. Its embedded Minion font has no usable Unicode mapping: ordinary get_text() returns control characters and find_tables() finds no table. The arm-count cells were checked against a memory-only rendered PDF crop and decoded into readable text. Their parentheses are age summaries and are not outcome SDs. An unmodified PDF-text quote checker may flag those count-table quotes despite their visual and glyph-level verification.
